seoTitle: How to See Previous Sprint History in Jira
metaDescription: Track completed sprints in Jira using sprint reports and burndown charts to analyze velocity, completed issues, and team performance.
intro: Reviewing what happened in past sprints is essential for understanding your team's velocity and spotting patterns over time. This guide shows how to access previous sprint history in Jira and use its built-in reports to analyze completed work.

steps.heading: Open completed sprint reports
steps.body: Navigate to your project's reports section and select the Sprint Report to view data from a previously completed sprint.

steps.heading: Review the burndown chart
steps.body: Check the burndown chart for that sprint to see how work was completed relative to the planned timeline.

steps.heading: Analyze completed work and velocity
steps.body: Look at which issues were completed, which were carried over, and how that compares to previous sprints' velocity.

steps.heading: Compare across multiple sprints
steps.body: Review several past sprints together to spot trends in team performance and estimate future sprint capacity.

steps.heading: Apply insights to future planning
steps.body: Use what you learn from sprint history to refine backlog grooming and sprint planning going forward.

faq.question: Where do I find past sprint reports in Jira?
faq.answer: Sprint reports are located in the Reports section of your Jira project, where you can select any completed sprint to review.

faq.question: Can I see which issues were not completed in a sprint?
faq.answer: Yes, the Sprint Report clearly shows issues that were completed versus those that were incomplete or moved to the next sprint.

faq.question: Does Jira calculate team velocity automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, Jira's Velocity Chart report aggregates completed story points across sprints to show your team's velocity trend.

faq.question: Is sprint history available on all Jira plans?
faq.answer: Sprint reporting is available on Jira Software plans that support Scrum boards; access may vary slightly by plan tier.
